headline: Data & Business Intelligence
description: Learn to translate raw data into real decisions. We cover the full modern data stack — from SQL fundamentals and Python automation to Power BI dashboards deployed in production.

tools.name: Excel
tools.definition: Microsoft's spreadsheet — still the most widely used data tool in the world, especially in enterprise.

tools.name: Google Sheets
tools.definition: Browser-based spreadsheets with real-time collaboration — great for lightweight data work and sharing.

tools.name: Airtable
tools.definition: A spreadsheet-database hybrid — structured data with a friendly UI, popular for no-code workflows.

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.definition: The most powerful open-source SQL database — handles complex queries, JSON, and scales well.

tools.name: MySQL
tools.definition: The world's most-used open-source database — fast, reliable, and the backbone of most web apps.

tools.name: SQL Server
tools.definition: Microsoft's enterprise database — common in corporate environments and integrates natively with Power BI.

tools.name: Oracle
tools.definition: Enterprise-grade database used by large corporations — powerful but expensive and complex to operate.

tools.name: SQLite
tools.definition: A lightweight file-based database — perfect for local apps, mobile, and rapid prototyping.

tools.name: Snowflake
tools.definition: Cloud data warehouse that separates storage and compute — pay per query, scales instantly.

tools.name: BigQuery
tools.definition: Google's serverless data warehouse — query terabytes of data with SQL in seconds.

tools.name: Amazon Redshift
tools.definition: AWS's columnar data warehouse built for large-scale analytics workloads.

tools.name: Azure Synapse
tools.definition: Microsoft's unified analytics platform combining SQL warehouse and Spark in one service.

tools.name: Databricks SQL
tools.definition: SQL layer on top of Databricks — run analytical queries against your data lakehouse.

tools.name: Databricks
tools.definition: Unified platform for data engineering, ML, and analytics — built on Apache Spark.

tools.name: Delta Lake
tools.definition: Open storage format that adds ACID transactions and versioning to your data lake.

tools.name: Apache Iceberg
tools.definition: Open table format for huge analytic datasets — enables time travel and schema evolution.

tools.name: Amazon S3
tools.definition: AWS object storage — the backbone of most cloud data lakes, storing files cheaply at scale.

tools.name: Azure Data Lake
tools.definition: Microsoft's cloud storage service optimised for big data analytics workloads.

tools.name: Fivetran
tools.definition: Automated pipelines that sync your SaaS tools and databases into your warehouse — no code required.

tools.name: Airbyte
tools.definition: Open-source EL tool with 300+ connectors — move data from any source to your warehouse.

tools.name: Stitch
tools.definition: Simple cloud ETL for developers — connects data sources to your warehouse in minutes.

tools.name: Matillion
tools.definition: Low-code ETL built for cloud warehouses — visual pipelines for Snowflake, BigQuery, and Redshift.

tools.name: Hevo Data
tools.definition: No-code real-time data pipeline that loads data from 150+ sources into your warehouse.

tools.name: dbt
tools.definition: Transforms raw warehouse data using SQL — handles testing, docs, and deployment of your data models.

tools.name: Dataform
tools.definition: Google's SQL-based transformation tool — similar to dbt, natively integrated with BigQuery.

tools.name: Coalesce
tools.definition: Visual data transformation platform purpose-built for Snowflake — drag-and-drop with SQL underneath.

tools.name: SQLMesh
tools.definition: Next-gen transformation framework with built-in testing, environments, and incremental models.

tools.name: Alteryx
tools.definition: No-code/low-code analytics automation — drag-and-drop workflow builder for data prep and blending.

tools.name: SQL
tools.definition: The language of data — used to query, filter, join, and aggregate data from any relational database.

tools.name: Python
tools.definition: The most versatile language for data work — used for cleaning, analysis, automation, and ML.

tools.name: R
tools.definition: Statistical computing language — preferred by data scientists for statistical analysis and visualisation.

tools.name: Julia
tools.definition: High-performance language for scientific computing — as fast as C but as readable as Python.

tools.name: Pandas
tools.definition: Python's core data manipulation library — load, clean, filter, and reshape any dataset with DataFrames.

tools.name: NumPy
tools.definition: Fast numerical computing in Python — the foundation beneath pandas, scipy, and machine learning.

tools.name: Polars
tools.definition: Lightning-fast DataFrame library written in Rust — 10-100x faster than pandas for large datasets.

tools.name: PySpark
tools.definition: Python API for Apache Spark — distributed data processing for datasets too large for one machine.

tools.name: DuckDB
tools.definition: In-process SQL analytics engine — query CSVs and Parquet files at Spark speeds, zero setup.

tools.name: Power BI
tools.definition: Microsoft's drag-and-drop dashboard tool — connects to any source and publishes reports across your org.

tools.name: Tableau
tools.definition: Industry-leading visual analytics — turns complex data into interactive, shareable dashboards.

tools.name: Looker Studio
tools.definition: Google's free dashboarding tool — connects to BigQuery, Sheets, and 800+ data sources.

tools.name: Qlik Sense
tools.definition: Associative analytics platform — lets users explore data relationships without predefined queries.

tools.name: Metabase
tools.definition: Open-source BI tool teams can self-host — lets non-technical users ask questions of their database.

tools.name: Apache Superset
tools.definition: Open-source data exploration and dashboarding — powerful, free alternative to Tableau.

tools.name: Matplotlib
tools.definition: Python's foundational plotting library — full control over every chart element, verbose but powerful.

tools.name: Seaborn
tools.definition: Statistical visualisation library built on Matplotlib — beautiful defaults for common chart types.

tools.name: Plotly
tools.definition: Interactive chart library for Python and JS — hover, zoom, and filter directly in the chart.

tools.name: Altair
tools.definition: Declarative visualisation library based on Vega-Lite — clean grammar for statistical charts.

tools.name: Bokeh
tools.definition: Interactive web-ready visualisations in Python — great for building dashboards in the browser.

tools.name: Mixpanel
tools.definition: Event-based product analytics — track exactly what users do in your app and build funnels.

tools.name: Amplitude
tools.definition: Product analytics platform focused on user behaviour — helps teams understand what drives retention.

tools.name: PostHog
tools.definition: Open-source product analytics with feature flags and session replay — self-hostable and privacy-friendly.

tools.name: Heap
tools.definition: Auto-captures every user interaction — no manual event tracking, retroactively analyse any behaviour.

tools.name: Google Analytics
tools.definition: Web analytics platform — tracks traffic, sessions, and conversions across your website.

tools.name: Jupyter
tools.definition: The standard interactive notebook for data science — mix code, output, and markdown in one document.

tools.name: Google Colab
tools.definition: Free cloud-hosted Jupyter notebooks with GPU access — no setup, runs straight in your browser.

tools.name: Hex
tools.definition: Collaborative data notebook with a polished app-publishing layer — built for data teams.

tools.name: Deepnote
tools.definition: Real-time collaborative data notebook — like Google Docs, but for data science.

tools.name: Observable
tools.definition: JavaScript-based reactive notebooks — best for interactive data visualisation in the browser.

tools.name: Apache Airflow
tools.definition: Python-based scheduler for data pipelines — define DAGs to run, monitor, and retry jobs automatically.

tools.name: Dagster
tools.definition: Modern data orchestration — asset-first approach with built-in lineage and observability.

tools.name: Prefect
tools.definition: Python-first workflow orchestration — simpler than Airflow with a clean UI and cloud option.

tools.name: Mage
tools.definition: Modern pipeline tool with a visual editor — combines notebook-style development with orchestration.

tools.name: Great Expectations
tools.definition: Python library for validating your data — write expectations, run tests automatically in your pipeline.

tools.name: Soda
tools.definition: SQL-based data quality testing — define checks in YAML and monitor your data contracts.

tools.name: Monte Carlo
tools.definition: Data observability platform — detects data incidents before they reach dashboards or models.

tools.name: Anomalo
tools.definition: AI-powered data quality monitoring — automatically learns your data patterns and alerts on anomalies.

tools.name: Telmai
tools.definition: No-code data observability — monitors pipelines and flags quality issues in real-time.

tools.name: Atlan
tools.definition: Active data catalogue — connects your data assets, lineage, and documentation in one searchable hub.

tools.name: Alation
tools.definition: Enterprise data catalogue — helps teams find, understand, and govern data assets across the org.

tools.name: Collibra
tools.definition: Data governance platform for large enterprises — manages data policies, ownership, and compliance.

tools.name: Microsoft Purview
tools.definition: Microsoft's unified data governance solution — maps and classifies data across Azure and beyond.

tools.name: DataHub
tools.definition: Open-source metadata platform from LinkedIn — discover and understand data assets across your stack.

tools.name: Hightouch
tools.definition: Syncs your warehouse data to CRMs, ad platforms, and 200+ destinations — no custom pipelines needed.

tools.name: Census
tools.definition: Pushes your warehouse models into Salesforce, HubSpot, and any SaaS tool your team uses.

tools.name: RudderStack
tools.definition: Open-source customer data platform — collects, transforms, and routes event data to any destination.

tools.name: Grouparoo
tools.definition: Open-source reverse ETL for syncing warehouse data to marketing and sales tools.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.definition: OpenAI's AI — used to write SQL, explain data, generate reports, and automate analysis workflows.

tools.name: Claude
tools.definition: Anthropic's AI — strong at reasoning through complex data problems and writing clean, documented code.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.definition: Google's multimodal AI — integrates with BigQuery and Sheets for AI-assisted data workflows.

tools.name: Power BI Copilot
tools.definition: Microsoft's AI layer in Power BI — generate reports and DAX measures using natural language.

tools.name: ThoughtSpot Sage
tools.definition: AI-powered search analytics — ask questions of your data in plain English, get instant answers.
